---
title: "Pankegg_app.py"
---
<br>

Pankegg's web server for interactive data exploration.

## Input file

Pankegg_app.py is using the output of [pankegg_make_db.py](Pankegg_make_db.qmd). 

## Usage APP

To start the Pankegg web server with your database, use the following command (replace with your actual database path):

```bash
pankegg_app --d /Path/to/YOUR_PANKEGG.db
```
(Replace /Path/to/YOUR_PANKEGG.db with your actual path. From a copy of the repository, `python pankegg_app.py --d ...` works too.)

> **Note:**  
> Before running the web application, it is highly recommended to **set your own Flask secret key**. Put `FLASK_SECRET_KEY=<a long random value>` in a `.env` file in the directory where you start `pankegg_app` (or one of its parent directories, or the repository folder), or export `FLASK_SECRET_KEY` in your shell. You can create the file with `python3 -c "import secrets; print('FLASK_SECRET_KEY=' + secrets.token_hex(32))" > .env`.
This key is used by Flask for session security. Leaving it as the default ('dev') is fine for local or testing use, but for any real-world or multi-user deployment, you should generate and use a strong, unique secret key to prevent session tampering and increase security.

## Parameters APP

- `--d` or `--database`  
Path to the SQLite database you want to browse.  
Example: `--d /Path/to/YOUR_PANKEGG.db`

- `--host`  
Address the web server listens on. The default, `127.0.0.1`, is reachable from your own computer only. Use `--host 0.0.0.0` to make the app reachable from other computers on your network (for example when it runs on a server).

- `--port`  
Port the web server listens on (default `5000`).

- `--debug`  
Flask debug mode, for development only. Do not combine it with `--host 0.0.0.0`: the debugger lets anyone who can reach the port run code on your computer.

- `--version`, `--help`  
Print the version, or a help message with all available options.

## Output APP

By default, the web server starts on your own computer (host `127.0.0.1`) and port `5000`.  
Once started, you can access the Pankegg interface in your browser by navigating to:

[http://127.0.0.1:5000](http://127.0.0.1:5000)

You will be able to browse, filter, and visualize all results contained in your selected database.

> Up to version 2.0.0 the app listened on every network interface (`0.0.0.0`) with the Flask debugger switched on. From 2.1.0 it is local and the debugger is off unless you ask for it. If you run Pankegg on a remote server, either start it with `--host 0.0.0.0` on a trusted network, or keep the default and forward the port over SSH: `ssh -L 5000:127.0.0.1:5000 user@server`.

## Run with Testdata


You can test the web interface using either the database provided with the repository, example databases from the test data, or your own generated databases.  
Here are example commands (replace BASH with the actual commands):

- To run the app on the example database installed with Pankegg (`pankegg/data/pankegg.db`, used when `--d` is not given):

```bash
pankegg_app
```

- To run the app on the example Sourmash test database (`pankegg_test_data/sourmash_example.db`):

```bash
pankegg_app --d pankegg_test_data/sourmash_example.db
```

- To run the app on the example GTDB-TK test database (`pankegg_test_data/gtdbtk_example.db`):

```bash
pankegg_app --d pankegg_test_data/gtdbtk_example.db
```

- To run the app on the Sourmash database you created during the test (`pankegg_test_data/test_sourmash.db`):

```bash
pankegg_app --d pankegg_test_data/test_sourmash.db
```

- To run the app on the GTDB-TK database you created during the test (`pankegg_test_data/test_gtdbtk.db`):

```bash
pankegg_app --d pankegg_test_data/test_gtdbtk.db
```
